A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIGA research, with matching algorithms, benchmarks and extensive retained results. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable. Internal reporting ambiguities can be assessed separately from material completeness.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative experiments on BlenderGym, SlideBench and BlenderBench, including appendix Tables 5–6, alongside qualitative reconstruction and simulation results.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional qualitative outputs and a sliding-window memory ablation in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The core synthesis–execution–inspection loop and sliding-window update remain. However, v3 newly lists init_scene and undo_action and describes SAM-3D initialization, while Appendix D retains the earlier tool schemas and separate-verifier behavior despite the main text's unified-agent description. The PDFs do not resolve actual procedural changes versus expanded or inconsistent documentation.

E1.justification: The three benchmarks and corresponding BlenderBench tracks remain despite track renaming. Qualitative physical scenarios change: conveyor-belt and billiards simulations in v1 Figure 4 are replaced by fruit collisions, mirror shattering and earthquake simulations in v3 Figure 8, extending the demonstrated physical task requirements.

E2.justification: The quantitative comparator sets remain unchanged: one-shot generation and BlenderAlchemy in the main graphics comparisons, and one-shot generation in the extended tables. v3 Figure 5 additionally compares against an unbounded-memory variant without sliding-window truncation.

E3.justification: BlenderBench's reported size changes from 30 instances, ten per track, to 27 tasks. Best-of-N is redescribed from samples per instruction to candidate edits selected at each step. SlideBench replaces separate reference-based/reference-free metrics with an undefined Quality score. These are reported protocol changes; reruns are not established, and v3's Claude-3.5 table label conflicts with its Sonnet-4 prose.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 5 adds a qualitative ablation testing sliding-window versus unbounded memory, showing loss of previously constructed objects without truncation. The earlier navigation and fine-grained grounding trajectories are retained as reorganized Figures 3–4 rather than constituting new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. Best-of-1/best-of-4 denotes candidate-search budgets rather than uncertainty estimation, and the new qualitative ablation adds no statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Corresponding main and appendix BlenderGym/BlenderBench numerical results match. v3 adds the memory-ablation outcome, additional scene/slide examples and replacement 4D outputs. SlideBench removes separate metric entries, reports Quality values and changes derived improvements, including Qwen's 443.38% to 446.7%; this does not establish improved underlying performance.

T1.justification: v1 Section 3.4 explicitly claims a computational-cost reduction from O(N²) to O(Nk); v3 removes this asymptotic argument. The sliding-window update remains in Algorithm 1. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: v3's introduction additionally claims to overcome complementary weaknesses of gradient-based inverse graphics and one-shot VLM generation. The central training-free, task/model-agnostic agent contribution, BlenderBench contribution and headline improvements of 35.32%, 117.17% and 124.70% remain.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands mechanism interpretations: semantic skills compress the action space, and physics-engine execution purportedly ensures strict physical accuracy and temporal consistency. Memory truncation is strengthened from having little impact to being inherently lossless. The specific inspection-tool limitation concerning missed fine geometry in v1's conclusion is omitted.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix C identifies GPT-4o as the VLM-score evaluator and supplies its prompt template, criteria and instructions for ignoring stylistic artifacts. Appendix B newly describes supplementary .blend files and .mp4 videos, whose availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Existing iteration limits, qualitative context window, GPT-5 backbone and tool schemas are largely retained.

R1.justification: v3 substantially reframes the motivation around complementary differentiable-graphics and VLM capabilities, adding references including DECA, Soft Rasterizer and OpenDR. Context Rot, Lost in the Middle and a semantic-skills guide additionally support its memory and interface positioning. This extends the earlier emphasis on unifying programmatic visual analysis and synthesis.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting. The method is reorganized around the reasoning loop, memory and semantic skills; BlenderBench moves ahead of the merged existing-benchmark discussion; and appendices gain subdivisions and expanded explanations. Generator/verifier terminology is extensively recast as agent phases.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. v3 reorganizes the skill table, adds the memory-ablation and slide-result figures, expands or replaces qualitative panels, redraws the benchmark overview and relocates existing trajectories. BlenderGym and SlideBench tables are compressed into adjacent displays, with SlideBench's columns restructured.

improvement.justification: The new memory ablation and evaluator prompt improve evidential support and reproducibility. However, v3 loses SlideBench's metric breakdown, introduces a Claude-3.5/Sonnet-4 inconsistency, and changes the benchmark count without explaining its relationship to unchanged scores. Stronger lossless-memory and physical-accuracy assertions also lack corresponding validation. These benefits and reporting weaknesses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
